generation_members.surface_form: Universal Machine Learning Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian for Materials
The universal HamGNN model achieves a mean absolute error of 5.4 meV for the real‑space Hamiltonian matrix on the test set after the first round of training.

The universal HamGNN model accurately predicts the energy band structures and charge densities of complex multi‑element crystals (e.g., Hf2Zr9Ta6Ti5Nb5B54, HfTaTiB4MoC4, K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F), matching DFT results.

High‑throughput screening of 188,722 GeNOME crystals with the universal model identifies 21,973 insulators (3,940 direct‑gap) and 5,109 flat‑band materials, nearly doubling the entries in the Materials Flatband Database.

Using the universal HamGNN model reduces computational cost by several orders of magnitude compared with DFT (e.g., 0.33 core·hours versus 181 core·hours for a large MOF) while preserving accuracy of band gaps and charge‑density differences.
A two‑step training procedure—first minimizing real‑space Hamiltonian error, then adding orbital‑energy error at random k‑points—is essential to obtain a truly universal Hamiltonian model.

Incorporating orbital‑energy loss in a second fine‑tuning round markedly improves band‑structure predictions, yielding energy bands and Fermi surfaces that closely match DFT calculations for the test set.

The universal HamGNN model generalizes to crystals containing more than five distinct elements and to any element supported by the OpenMX PBE pseudopotential library, effectively covering the entire periodic table.
The PBE functional combined with PAW potentials is the default exchange-correlation functional and potential combination for ICSD, Binary Alloy, and Heusler databases.
The applied plane-wave kinetic energy cut-off (Ecut) is the largest recommended value among all species in the calculation, increased by a factor of 1.4.
DFT+U corrections are applied to the entire ICSD database and certain Heusler database entries containing O, S, Se, and F elements, but not to the Binary Alloy database.

Specific Ueff parameters are defined for d-block elements (Table 4) and U, J parameters for f-block elements (Table 5) to correct self-interaction error in DFT+U calculations, with values ranging from 1.9 eV (In) to 7.5 eV (Zn).

The first RELAX calculation is performed in collinear spin-polarized fashion with initial magnetic moments set to 1.0 µB per atom, and spin polarization is turned off in subsequent calculations if magnetization is below 0.025 µB/atom.

Electronic convergence criteria are δEelec = 10⁻⁵ eV and ionic convergence criteria are δEion = 10⁻⁴ eV for Elements database entries, while all other databases use δEelec = 10⁻³ eV and δEion = 10⁻² eV.

Following the AFLOW standard enables materials science researchers to reproduce AFLOWLIB consortium results and make direct comparisons of properties between different materials for identifying trends and formulating design rules.
The AFLOWLIB data is accessible through a REST-API for standardized data exchange.
FastCHGNet trains in 1.5 hours using 32 GPUs compared to 8.3 days on a single A100 GPU for the original CHGNet model.
CHGNet achieves test mean absolute errors of 29 meV/atom for energy, 70 meV/Angstrom for force, and 0.308 GPa for stress.
M3GNet achieves test mean absolute errors of 35 meV/atom for energy, 72 meV/Angstrom for force, and 0.41 GPa for stress.
CHGNet uniquely includes electronic effects of valences by explicitly embedding magnetic moments on the vector representation of each atom, enabling charge-informed atomistic simulations.
CHGNet achieved the lowest formation energy MAE at 81 meV/atom, while all other models had MAEs of 129 meV/atom or higher.
M3GNet is an extension of MEGNet model to include 3-body interactions, explicit atomic coordinates, and 3×3 crystal lattice matrix.
M3GNet potential covers 89 elements with no particular constraints on applicability, though training has strong bias toward solid phases.
Including magnetic moments in CHGNet training led to error reductions of 1-10% for energy, force, and stress compared to not including magnetic moments.
